gated pulse train: the input is a subtract comparator's rear; its output returns to its side through dust and a delay-1 repeater, so it pulses every 8 gt while the input is on (the first pulse 2 gt after it) and stops within 2 gt of the release

burst 2: a copper bulb toggles on each rising edge, its comparator changes, an observer makes that a 2 gt pulse, a delay-3 repeater stretches it to 6 gt, and a second observer pulses on both of the repeater's edges: 2 pulses 6 gt apart for any input length (min-pulse 1)

burst 3: the 2-pulse bulb burst (bulb, comparator, observer, delay-3 repeater, observer) plus an observer cascade: an observer watching the second observer toggles a second bulb, and two more observers turn that into a third pulse 6 gt after the second (found by local search from a 20-block tap design)

burst 4: a bulb edge detector (bulb, comparator, observer) whose pulse fans out through observers, a second bulb and a torch into delayed taps that all end in the output cell: four 2 gt pulses for any input length (found by local search from a 32-block design with three repeater taps)

gated pulse train in 3 blocks: the input extends a sticky piston that pushes an observer face to face with another; the two observers chase each other (each fires on the other's change), a 2 gt pulse every 4 gt at the output, until the piston pulls the observer away (the fastest and smallest gated clock: P 4 gt)

burst 2 in 9 blocks: a bulb edge detector (bulb, comparator, observer) and a repeater hold a sticky piston out for a fixed time; the piston pushes an observer face to face with another and the two chase each other (a 2 gt pulse every 4 gt) until it pulls back: 2 pulses for any input length

burst 3 in 9 blocks: a bulb edge detector (bulb, comparator, observer) and a repeater hold a sticky piston out for a fixed time; the piston pushes an observer face to face with another and the two chase each other (a 2 gt pulse every 4 gt) until it pulls back: 3 pulses for any input length

Lights the output only after the input has stayed on for 10 ticks, and turns it off the moment the input stops: the input reaches the output only through a stone that a sticky piston slides into place after a repeater delay, so short pulses never get through. Details: the input's dust points into the empty cell beside the output; a delay-3 repeater (6 ticks) and two dust power the sticky piston, so an input shorter than the repeater delay plus the piston's travel never lights the output. The repeater makes every piston pulse at least 4 ticks, so the piston never spits its stone.

Keeps its output on for 12 ticks after the input turns off: two comparators pass the signal around a small loop, and the dust in the loop weakens it on every lap until it dies out. Details: 5 dust carry the second comparator's output back to the first, losing 4 signal strength per 4-tick lap; while the input is on it keeps the loop full; the comparator the output reads sets the exact length.

Gives a 12-tick output pulse after each input pulse, and a new input restarts the 12 ticks: every input refills a small two-comparator loop that fades out on its own. Details: a copper bulb, a comparator and two observers turn each rising edge into 4 ticks of full-strength signal for the loop; 6 dust carry the signal back around, losing 5 per 4-tick lap. A short pulse needs a lossier, longer return line, which is why the short versions take more blocks than the long ones.

Keeps the output on for 108 ticks after the input turns off (a long off-delay): a small fast loop keeps a bigger, slower loop topped up, and once the input is gone the big loop counts down; each extra pair of comparators in the big loop adds 56 ticks. Details: stage 1 is a two-comparator loop (4-tick lap) that the input holds full; once the input stops it decays 2 per lap, so its output lasts at least 28 ticks. A repeater reading it powers stage 2, a three-comparator loop (6-tick lap) that loses only 1 per lap; stage 1's long output refills it evenly at full strength, and once stage 1 dies stage 2 counts its 15 levels down and the output goes dark at 0.

Gives a 116-tick output pulse after each input pulse, and a new input restarts it (a long retriggerable one-shot): each input fills a small fast loop that keeps a bigger, slower loop topped up, which then counts down; each extra pair of comparators in the big loop adds 56 ticks. Details: a copper bulb, a comparator and two observers turn each rising edge into 4 ticks of full-strength signal for stage 1, a two-comparator loop (4-tick lap) that decays 2 per lap, so its output lasts at least 28 ticks; a repeater reading it refills stage 2, a three-comparator loop (6-tick lap) that loses only 1 per lap, which then counts its 15 levels down.

Gives one 14-tick output pulse per input pulse and ignores new inputs until it has finished: the input refills a small fading loop through a gate that the loop keeps shut while it runs. Details: a copper bulb, a comparator, an observer and a delay-3 repeater turn each rising edge into a 6-tick charge through a subtract comparator; the loop's own signal feeds that comparator's side, so edges during the pulse pass nothing; 6 dust return the signal, losing 5 per 4-tick lap (a short pulse needs a lossier, longer line, hence more blocks).
